'''Maurice Sidney Skolnick''' is a British physicist and Emeritus Professor of Experimental Condensed Matter Physics at the [[University of Sheffield]]. His research concerns the optoelectronic properties of semiconductor materials and nanostructures, including quantum dots, semiconductor microcavities and photonic crystals.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Blinnikova |first=Natalia |date=2017-05-11 |title=Royal Society Member Maurice Skolnick: Why Making Science Understandable to Society Matters |url=https://news.itmo.ru/en/news/6644/null/ |access-date=2026-09-01 |website=news.itmo.ru |language=ru}}</ref>

He was elected a [[Fellow of the Royal Society]] in 2009 and a foreign member of the [[Russian Academy of Sciences]] in 2011.<ref name="RoyalSociety">{{cite web |title=Maurice Skolnick |website=Royal Society |url=https://royalsociety.org/people/maurice-skolnick-12291/ |access-date=4 August 2026}}</ref>

==Education==

In 1972, Skolnick obtained a BSc with first-class honours at the [[University of Oxford]].<ref name="Sheffield">{{cite web |title=Professor Maurice Skolnick |website=University of Sheffield |url=https://sheffield.ac.uk/mps/people/honorary/maurice-skolnick |access-date=4 August 2026}}</ref> In 1975, he completed a PhD. His doctoral thesis, supervised by [[R. A. Stradling]], was titled ''Infrared Studies of Semiconductors''.<ref name="Sheffield" />

==Career==

Skolnick spent two years as a postdoctoral researcher at the [[Max Planck Institute for Solid State Research]].<ref name="Sheffield" /> In 1978, he moved to the [[Royal Signals and Radar Establishment]] (RSRE) in Malvern, where he worked for thirteen years.<ref name="Sheffield" /> In 1984, he was also a visiting scientist at [[Bell Laboratories]].<ref name="RoyalSociety" />

In January 1991, Skolnick was appointed Professor of Condensed Matter Physics at the University of Sheffield, a position he held until his retirement.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2026-05-01 |title=Celebrating a Legacy of Excellence: 35 Years of LDSD |url=https://sheffield.ac.uk/quantum/news/celebrating-legacy-excellence-35-years-ldsd |access-date=2026-09-01 |website=sheffield.ac.uk |language=en}}</ref> He became Emeritus Professor in September 2025.<ref name="Sheffield" /> At Sheffield, he headed the university's semiconductor physics research group.<ref>{{Cite web |title=University of Sheffield launches Sheffield Quantum Centre ⋆ Electronics Weekly |url=https://www.electronicsweekly.com/news/research-news/university-sheffield-launches-sheffield-quantum-centre-2020-02/ |access-date=2026-09-01 |language=en}}</ref> He has also served as Research Director, and previously as deputy and co-director, of the EPSRC National Centre for III–V Technologies at Sheffield, later renamed the National Epitaxy Facility.<ref name="RoyalSociety" /><ref name="Sheffield" />

Skolnick was chair of the Semiconductor Commission and a vice-president of the [[International Union of Pure and Applied Physics]] from 2002 to 2005.<ref>{{Cite web |title=IUPAP: Germany 2002 Meeting Minutes |url=https://archive.iupap.org/exec/minutes/02-germany-comm.html |access-date=2026-09-01 |website=archive.iupap.org}}</ref> He held an EPSRC Senior Research Fellowship from 2001 to 2006 and received a five-year [[European Research Council]] Advanced Investigator Grant in 2012.<ref name="Sheffield" />

==Research==

Skolnick used cyclotron resonance techniques to study the band structure of III–V semiconductors, including the valence band of [[gallium arsenide]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Skolnick |first=M S |last2=Jain |first2=A K |last3=Stradling |first3=R A |last4=Leotin |first4=J |last5=Ousset |first5=J C |date=1976-07-28 |title=An investigation of the anisotropy of the valence band of GaAs by cyclotron resonance |url=https://iopscience.iop.org/article/10.1088/0022-3719/9/14/019 |journal=Journal of Physics C: Solid State Physics |volume=9 |issue=14 |pages=2809–2821 |doi=10.1088/0022-3719/9/14/019 |issn=0022-3719}}</ref> In the late 1970s, while working at the Max Planck Institute with D. Bimberg, he contributed to experimental studies of electron–hole liquids in compound semiconductors.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Bimberg |first=D. |last2=Skolnick |first2=M. S. |last3=Choyke |first3=W. J. |date=1978-01-02 |title=Observation of an Electron-Hole Liquid in Cubic SiC |url=https://doi.org/10.1103/physrevlett.40.56 |journal=Physical Review Letters |volume=40 |issue=1 |pages=56–60 |doi=10.1103/physrevlett.40.56 |issn=0031-9007|url-access=subscription }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last=Skolnick |first=M.S. |last2=Bimberg |first2=D. |last3=Choyke |first3=W.J. |date=1978 |title=The electron-hole-liquid in 15R-SiC |url=https://doi.org/10.1016/0038-1098(78)90175-8 |journal=Solid State Communications |volume=28 |issue=10 |pages=865–868 |doi=10.1016/0038-1098(78)90175-8 |issn=0038-1098|url-access=subscription }}</ref>

He contributed to work on magnetic-field-induced indirect gaps in semiconductor systems with D. M. Whittaker.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Whittaker |first1=D. M. |last2=Fisher |first2=T. A. |last3=Simmonds |first3=P. E. |last4=Skolnick |first4=M. S. |last5=Smith |first5=R. S. |year=1991 |title=Magnetic-field-induced indirect gap in a modulation-doped quantum well |url=https://journals.aps.org/prl/abstract/10.1103/PhysRevLett.67.887 |journal=Physical Review Letters |volume=67 |issue=7 |pages=887–890 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.67.887}}</ref> He also contributed to research on many-body effects, including the Fermi edge singularity and Fermi-sea shake-up in modulation-doped quantum wells, and reported an early observation of population inversion in semiconductor quantum wells using resonant-tunnelling techniques with J. W. Cockburn.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Cockburn |first=J. W. |last2=Skolnick |first2=M. S. |last3=Whittaker |first3=D. M. |last4=Buckle |first4=P. D. |last5=Willcox |first5=A. R. K. |last6=Smith |first6=G. W. |date=1994-05-02 |title=Evidence for population inversion in excited electron states of a double barrier resonant tunneling structure |url=https://doi.org/10.1063/1.111627 |journal=Applied Physics Letters |volume=64 |issue=18 |pages=2400–2402 |doi=10.1063/1.111627 |issn=0003-6951|url-access=subscription }}</ref>

From 1995 onwards, Skolnick worked on the physics of exciton-polaritons in semiconductor microcavities, including electric-field and temperature tuning of exciton-photon coupling.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Physicists control transitions between different states of matter |url=https://phys.org/news/2018-04-physicists-transitions-states.html |website=Phys.org}}</ref> His Sheffield group, in collaboration with J. J. Baumberg, reported continuous-wave stimulated scattering in semiconductor microcavities in 2000.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Stevenson |first1=R. M. |last2=Astratov |first2=V. ==AegiQ==

In December 2019, Skolnick was one of four co-founders of AegiQ, a quantum photonics spin-out company from the University of Sheffield, alongside Maksym Sich, Scott Dufferwiel and Jon Heffernan.<ref>{{cite web |title=UK Startup and Spin-out From The University of Sheffield Has Photonics Ambitions |website=The Quantum Insider |date=21 June 2020 |url=https://thequantuminsider.com/2020/06/21/uk-startup-and-spin-out-from-the-university-of-sheffield-photonics-ambitions/ |access-date=4 August 2026}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Moore |first=Kim |date=2025-11-03 |title=9 photonics spinouts that can speed up AI data centres and quantum |url=https://globalventuring.com/corporate/industrial/9-photonics-spinouts-ai-data-centres-quantum/ |access-date=2026-09-01 |website=Global Venturing}}</ref> The company develops single-photon sources and photonic quantum-computing hardware based on research originating at the University of Sheffield.<ref>{{cite web |title=Accelerating quantum technology worldwide |website=University of Sheffield |url=https://sheffield.ac.uk/research/features/aegiq-quantum-technology |access-date=4 August 2026}}</ref>

==Awards and honours==

* [[Mott Medal and Prize]] of the [[Institute of Physics]] (2002), for contributions to the understanding of excitons, defects and interactions in semiconductors.<ref name=":0">{{cite web |title=Optics and Photonics Prize |website=Institute of Physics |url=https://www.iop.org/physics-community/special-interest-groups/quantum-electronics-photonics-group/optics-photonics-prize |access-date=4 August 2026}}</ref>
* Elected [[Fellow of the Royal Society]] (2009).<ref name="RoyalSociety" />
* Foreign Member of the [[Russian Academy of Sciences]] (2011).<ref name="RoyalSociety" />
* Optics and Photonics Prize of the Institute of Physics (2018), for work on coupled light-matter systems and quantum optical circuits based on semiconductor quantum dots.<ref name=":0" />
